'''Primary batteries''' are a class of [[solid oxide fuel cell]]s that cannot be easily charged due to the poor reversibility of their discharging reactions.
They are notably

* relatively stable: the electrolyte is most commonly a solid paste (e.g, $KOH$)
** hence the common name '''dry cells''';
* cheap to produce;
* have good capacity and often higher voltage than rechargeable counterparts.

<ref>{{#cite:Q4245}}</ref>

== Limitations ==

* The collection and recycling of waste batteries requires a significant amount of effort
** the cost of which is seldom covered by the manufacturers
** leading to a poor lifecycle energy efficiency (<2%)
** many batteries end up in the landfill, causing sometimes serious soil pollution from heavy metal.

<ref>{{#cite:Q4245}}</ref>
